question: A 72-year-old male visits his gastroenterologist for a check-up one year following resection of a 2-cm malignant lesion in his sigmoid colon. Serum levels of which of the following can be used in this patient to test for cancer recurrence?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Resection of malignant lesion in sigmoid colon" -> "Increased risk for cancer recurrence" -> "Monitoring tumor markers for recurrence" -> 80% CHAIN: "Resection of malignant lesion in sigmoid colon" -> "Elevated carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) levels" -> "Indicator of cancer recurrence" -> 70% CHAIN: "Resection of malignant lesion in sigmoid colon" -> "CA-19-9 tumor marker" -> "Useful in monitoring colorectal cancer recurrence" -> 80%
analysis: Carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) is a tumor marker commonly used to monitor for cancer recurrence in patients with colorectal cancer. It is particularly useful in monitoring patients following resection of colorectal cancer, such as in this case of a 72-year-old male with a history of sigmoid colon cancer. CEA levels can help detect early signs of cancer recurrence.
